title: In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts, stop a fixed-width truncation from cutting a file path in h
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts, stop a fixed-width truncation from cutting a file path in half.

On line 2670 there is exactly one occurrence of this fragment:
.slice(0, 400),

Replace that fragment with:
.slice(0, 400).replace(/^(.{400})$/s, (_m, t) => t.replace(/\s\S*$/, "")),

That is the entire change: one file, one op, a suffix appended to an existing call. Do not restructure the line, do not touch any other line, and do not touch any other file.

WHY. That line builds a child-gap goal as "investigate and decompose gap " + parentId + ": " + parentSummary.slice(0, 400). Measured today on gap route-edit-098185ac: the 102-character prefix plus the 400-character body produced a summary of exactly 502 characters, and the cut landed inside a file extension, turning the real path repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/learning-signal-health-observer.ts into learning-signal-health-observer.t (one character short). The classifier then stored that as classification_metadata.edit_site, so a compose was routed at a file that does not exist, examined 0 of 1 staged files, and broke rung 2 of the operational_state ladder.

The new code changes nothing when no truncation occurred: the regex only matches when the sliced string is exactly 400 characters long, which happens only when the slice actually cut. In that case it drops the trailing partial token so the summary ends on a whitespace boundary instead of mid-path. The s flag is required because summaries contain newlines. A truncation that is merely lossy for prose is a correctness bug for a path, because a half-path is still syntactically a valid path and every downstream validator accepts it.
